summary: Takatsugu Hayashi works in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied at the University of Delhi (attested 1996). He held posts at Tohoku University (attested 1997), Sendai National College of Technology (attested 2008), and Hosen Gakuen College (attested 2015).

Takayasu Higuchi (1919–2015) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Kyoto University (~1939–1942), he later served as Professor of Archaeology there (~1964–1983) and directed several research institutes and museums.

Takayasu Kimura (born 1934) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Taisho University, later serving there as a lecturer (attested 1995), after working as a research assistant at the University of Tokyo (attested 1973–1978).

Takayasu Suzuki (born 1964) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1983–1993) and served as a professor at Yamaguchi Prefectural University (attested 2014–2015).

Takayoshi Kamei (1886–1977) specialized in history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1907–1910), where he later taught and instructed Hajime Nakamura, before holding posts at Ibaraki University (~1949–1957) and Seisen University (~1957–1968).

Takayoshi Namikawa (born 1947) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his undergraduate and graduate education at Bukkyo University, where he became a professor in 1981 and professor emeritus in 2018.

Takayuki Hirosawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He held positions at Taisho University, serving as a group member through 1991 and later as professor (attested 2014).

Takehiro Sueki (1921–2007) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1941–1944). He subsequently held academic posts at the University of Electro-Communications (~1951–1968), the University of Tokyo (~1968–1982), and Toyo University (~1982–1992).

Takeo Hibino (1914–2007) was a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1933–1936), held posts there and at its Institute for Research in Humanities (1936–1977), and later served as professor and president at Otemae University.

Takeo Kanaseki (1897–1983) was a researcher in history, archaeology, and other fields who studied at Kyoto University (~1919–1923). He held posts at Kyushu University (~1949–1960), Tottori University (~1960–1968), and Tezukayama Gakuin University (~1968–1979).
Takeo Warita (born 1944) is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied at Toyo University under Giyu Nishi.

Takeshi Fujii (born 1955) is an Indologist, historian, and archaeologist. He studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and the University of Delhi, then spent his career at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies from 1987 until becoming professor emeritus in 2021.

Takeshi Karashima (1903–1967) was a sinologist who studied at Tokyo Imperial University (~1923–1926). His career included positions at Keijo Imperial University (~1931–1945), Sagami Women's University, Showa Women's University, and Kamakura's library.

Takeshi Umehara (1925–2019) worked in philosophy, Japanology, and religious studies, studying at Kyoto University under Tokuryu Yamauchi. He held posts at Ritsumeikan University, Kyoto City University of Arts, and served as director of the International Research Center for Japanese Studies.

Takeshiro Kuraishi (1897–1975) was a scholar of sinology and linguistics who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1918–1921). He served as a professor at Kyoto University (~1940–1949), taught at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1958), and chaired Chugokugo Gakkai.

Takezo Kaneko (1905–1987) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1926–1929) under Tetsuro Watsuji. He held academic posts at Hokkaido University (~1947–1950), the University of Tokyo (~1950–1966), and International Christian University (~1966–1976).

Taklung Tsetrul Rinpoche (1926–2015) was a figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Po Lu Khenpo Dorjé. He taught Keith Dowman and Phakchok Rinpoche, and succeeded Trulshik Rinpoche Ngawang Chökyi Lodrö in 2012.

Takudo Ishikawa specializes in Buddhist studies. His career includes appointments as a research fellow at the Jodo Shu Research Institute (attested 2005–2006) and as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 2015).

Takushu Sugimoto (born 1935) specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He earned his degrees at Tohoku University, studying under Ensho Kanakura, Hakuyu Hadano, and others, and served as professor and professor emeritus at Kanazawa University.
Tamara Cohen is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed her PhD at the University of Toronto in 2023. Her doctoral supervisors were Srilata Raman and Jürgen Hanneder.
